title: TEDDY Framework: An Efficient Framework for Target Tracking Using Edge-Based Distributed Smart Cameras with Dynamic Camera SelectionTEDDY Framework: An Efficient Framework for Target Tracking Using Edge-Based Distributed Smart Cameras with Dynamic Camera Selection
content: This paper introduces a novel framework for a target tracking system with dynamic resource management using edge-based distributed smart cameras— the TEDDY framework. The proposed framework employs context-aware dynamic camera selection, activating only the cameras most likely to detect the target based on its predicted trajectory. This approach significantly reduces computational load and energy consumption while maintaining high tracking accuracy. Designed for resource-constrained environments, the framework offers a scalable solution for applications such as smart city infrastructure and emergency response systems. The framework was evaluated through two experiments. In the first, single-person tracking was conducted across multiple routes featuring various behaviors such as walking, running, and staggering, demonstrating the framework's effectiveness in optimizing resource utilization. In the second, the framework was applied to a simulated urban traffic light adjustment system for emergency vehicles, achieving significant reductions in computational load while maintaining equivalent tracking accuracy compared to an always-on camera system. These findings highlight the robustness, scalability, and energy efficiency of the TEDDY framework in edge-based camera networks. Furthermore, the TEDDY framework lays the groundwork for future advancements in dynamic resource management and tracking technologies, offering opportunities for integration into larger-scale systems and diverse operational scenarios.
